Front: What is the default file format for a modern PowerPoint presentation?
Back: pptx (Presentation Open XML). Older binary format is pptx's predecessor ppt
Category: and macro-enabled decks are saved as pptm.

Front: What keyboard shortcut inserts a new slide?
Back: Ctrl+M inserts a new slide below the current one in Normal view.

Front: What is the fastest way to duplicate a slide?
Back: Select the slide thumbnail and press Ctrl+D (or right-click > Duplicate Slide).

Front: What is the difference between F5 and Shift+F5?
Back: F5 starts the slide show from the first slide. Shift+F5 starts it from the currently selected slide.

Front: How do you exit a running slide show?
Back: Press Esc. The slide show also ends after the last slide unless Loop mode is on.

Front: What is Normal view used for?
Back: It is the main editing view with the slide pane
column5: used to build and edit individual slides.

Front: What is Slide Sorter view?
Back: A grid of slide thumbnails for reordering
column4: or applying transitions to many slides at once.

Front: What is Reading View?
Back: It plays the slide show in the window with simple controls
Category: useful for reviewing a deck without going full screen.

Front: What is a placeholder?
Back: An empty container on a slide layout (title
column5: chart) that prompts you to click and add content.

Front: What are slide layouts?
Back: Predefined arrangements of placeholders in the slide master (Title Slide
column4: Two Content) that keep slides consistent.

Front: What are Sections and what are they for?
Back: Named groups in the thumbnail rail that organize large decks
column4: and can be collapsed or reordered as a block.

Front: How do you promote or demote a bullet level in the Outline pane?
Back: Place the cursor in the line and press Tab to demote (deeper level) or Shift+Tab to promote (move up a level).

Front: What do Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y do?
Back: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action and Ctrl+Y redoes it or repeats the last command.

Front: How do you save a deck as a PDF?
Back: File > Save As (or Export) and choose PDF
Category: or File > Export > Create PDF/XPS Document.

Front: What is AutoSave and what does it require?
Back: AutoSave saves changes continuously to OneDrive or SharePoint. It is disabled for files stored only on the local machine.

Front: What is the Slide Master?
Back: The top-level template that stores theme colors
column5: and layouts for the whole presentation so global edits happen in one place.

Front: How do you open the Slide Master?
Back: View tab > Slide Master. Click Close Master View on the ribbon when finished.

Front: What is the difference between a theme and a template?
Back: A theme is a set of colors
column4: and effects. A template is a theme plus saved content and layouts

Front: What is the hierarchy of PowerPoint formatting?
Back: Theme > Slide Master > individual Layouts > individual slides. Formatting set at a higher level flows down to everything below it.

Front: Name the placeholder types managed in the master.
Back: Title
column6: and slide number placeholders. Footer items are switched on via Insert > Header & Footer.

Front: How do you apply a footer and slide numbers to every slide?
Back: Insert > Header & Footer

Front: How do you change theme colors for the whole deck?
Back: Design tab > Variants > Colors > Customize Colors
Category: then edit accent and text colors and save as a custom color set.

Front: How do you set a background for all slides?
Back: Right-click a slide > Format Background (or Design > Format Background). Hide background graphics on one slide by checking Hide background graphics in Format Background.

Front: What is the difference between the Notes Master and the Handout Master?
Back: Notes Master controls printed speaker notes pages. Handout Master controls printed handouts with 1

Front: Why edit the Slide Master instead of each slide?
Back: One edit to the master updates every slide and layout at once
column4: and prevents drift as the deck grows.

Front: How do you save a custom template?
Back: File > Save As and choose PowerPoint Template (potx). New presentations can then start from it via File > New > Personal.

Front: What is a theme variant and where do you find it?
Back: Design tab > Variants are coordinated color
column4: and effect sets that restyle the whole deck in one click while keeping layouts intact. Use the dropdowns to customize each aspect.

Front: What is the 6x6 rule?
Back: No more than 6 bullets per slide and 6 words per bullet. It keeps slides scannable and stops the audience reading instead of listening.

Front: What is the difference between a typeface and a font?
Back: A typeface is the design family (Arial). A font is a specific size and weight of that typeface (Arial Bold 24pt).

Front: Should slides use serif or sans-serif type?
Back: Sans-serif (Arial
column4: Helvetica) reads better on screen at large sizes. Serif type is traditionally used for dense printed body text.

Front: What is the minimum recommended body text size on a slide?
Back: 24pt for body text and 36pt or larger for titles. If text must shrink below 24pt

Front: How many typefaces should a deck use?
Back: Two at most: one for headings and one for body text. Extra weights and sizes create variety without adding visual noise.

Front: What contrast ratio should slide text meet for readability?
Back: WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Dark text on a light background or its inverse beats low-contrast pairings.

Front: What are complementary colors?
Back: Two colors opposite each other on the color wheel (blue and orange). They create strong contrast and work for emphasis.

Front: What are analogous colors?
Back: Three neighboring colors on the color wheel (blue
column4: green). They feel harmonious and work for backgrounds and calm themes.

Front: What is the difference between RGB and CMYK?
Back: RGB is additive light for screens (red
column4: blue). CMYK is subtractive ink for print (cyan

Front: What is the 60-30-10 color rule?
Back: About 60% dominant neutral
column4: and 10% accent for emphasis. The accent highlights only what matters most.

Front: What is visual hierarchy in slide design?
Back: Arranging elements so the eye reads them in order of importance using size
column5: and position. The headline is always read first.

Front: Why does alignment matter in slide layout?
Back: Aligned elements look intentional and professional. Use Align tools and smart guides (Alt-drag or View > Guides) rather than placing by eye.

Front: What is the principle of proximity?
Back: Items that belong together should sit close together. Related bullets
column4: and captions group into clear visual units.

Front: What does consistency mean in a deck?
Back: Same fonts
column6: and layout logic on every slide. Consistency signals professionalism and reduces mental load.

Front: What is white space and why is it valuable?
Back: The empty area around and between elements. It separates groups
column4: and makes slides look premium rather than crammed.

Front: How does the Z-pattern apply to slides?
Back: The eye scans a slide left to right and top to bottom in a rough Z. Place the title top-left
column4: and the takeaway or logo at the bottom.

Front: How do you keep color choices colorblind-friendly?
Back: Never rely on red versus green alone to show meaning. Add labels
column4: or position cues so meaning survives without color.

Front: How do you match a color already used in the deck?
Back: Shape Fill (or Text Fill) > Eyedropper
Category: then click the target color on the slide to sample it exactly.

Front: How do you insert a table?
Back: Insert > Table and drag to pick rows and columns
Category: or use Insert > Table > Insert Table and type the exact numbers.

Front: When should you use a table instead of a chart?
Back: Use a table for exact values and lookups the audience must read. Use a chart when the audience should see a trend

Front: What is a column chart best for?
Back: Comparing values across a few categories (quarterly revenue by region). Use a bar chart instead when category labels are long.

Front: What is a line chart best for?
Back: Showing change over continuous time (monthly signups across a year). Keep it to 4 or fewer series so lines stay readable.

Front: What is the recommended maximum number of pie chart slices?
Back: Five or fewer. Above that
Category: switch to a bar chart because small slices are impossible to compare.

Front: Why use a horizontal bar chart for long category names?
Back: Horizontal bars give long labels room to read left to right without rotating text or cramming columns.

Front: What is a scatter (XY) chart used for?
Back: Plotting the relationship between two numeric variables (ad spend vs sales) to reveal correlation or outliers.

Front: How do you merge cells in a table?
Back: Select the cells and click Table Layout > Merge Cells (or right-click > Merge Cells).

Front: How do you make table rows or columns equal in size?
Back: Select them and use Table Layout > Distribute Rows or Distribute Columns.

Front: How should a table header row look?
Back: Bold or a contrasting fill so it separates from data
Category: and repeat it across pages in printed handouts via Table Layout > Repeat Header Rows.

Front: What is zebra striping in tables?
Back: Alternating light row shading that helps the eye track across wide tables. Use subtle tints

Front: What are chart elements in PowerPoint?
Back: Title
column7: and trendlines. Add or remove them from Chart Design > Add Chart Element.

Front: How do you edit the data behind a chart?
Back: Chart Design > Edit Data opens the embedded worksheet (a trimmed Excel sheet). Type new values and the chart updates live.

Front: What is chart junk and how do you remove it?
Back: Unnecessary ink like heavy gridlines
column4: and redundant labels. Delete gridlines and 3D styles so the data is the only ink left.

Front: When should you use data labels instead of a value axis?
Back: Use direct data labels on bars when you need exact values on a handful of points. Otherwise keep the axis and skip labels to reduce clutter.

Front: How do you animate a chart piece by piece?
Back: Add an entrance effect to the chart
Category: then in Effect Options choose By Series or By Category (and By Element in Series if needed).

Front: When is SmartArt a better choice than a chart?
Back: SmartArt shows process
column5: org charts). Charts show numeric comparison and trends.

Front: What do table styles control?
Back: A preset combination of banding
column4: and border treatment. Apply one from Table Design and turn Banded Rows on or off there.

Front: What is the difference between a transition and an animation?
Back: A transition plays when moving between slides. An animation plays on an object inside a single slide.

Front: Name the four animation effect types.
Back: Entrance (object appears)
column5: and Motion Path (object moves along a drawn path).

Front: What is the Animation Pane and how do you open it?
Back: The sidebar that lists every effect in order with timing bars. Open it from Animations > Animation Pane.

Front: What are the three Start options for an animation?
Back: On Click
Category: With Previous (starts with the prior effect)
column4: and After Previous (starts when the prior effect finishes).

Front: What is a Trigger in PowerPoint animation?
Back: An effect that starts only when you click a specific object or play a media bookmark
Category: set under Trigger > On Click of.

Front: What is the difference between Duration and Delay?
Back: Duration is how long the effect plays. Delay is how long it waits before starting

Front: What does the Morph transition do?
Back: It animates objects between two slides by interpolating shared objects
column5: and color shifts. Duplicate a slide

Front: How do you apply one transition to the whole deck?
Back: Set the transition on one slide in the Transitions tab and click Apply To All.

Front: What is the Animation Painter?
Back: In the Animations tab
Category: it copies all animation effects from one object to another
column4: like Format Painter for animations. Double-click it to paint multiple objects.

Front: What do Effect Options control?
Back: The variant of a chosen effect

Front: How do you make a slide advance without clicking?
Back: Transitions tab > Timing > Advance Slide: uncheck On Mouse Click and check After
Category: then set the time in seconds.

Front: What is Rehearse Timings?
Back: Slide Show > Rehearse Timings runs the deck with a stopwatch so PowerPoint records how long you spend on each slide and can auto-advance with those timings.

Front: How do you set transition direction and sound?
Back: Transitions tab > Effect Options picks the direction. The Sound dropdown adds a sound
Category: which should normally stay (No Sound) for business decks.

Front: Why avoid flashy transitions in a business deck?
Back: Spin
column4: and similar effects distract from content and can look unprofessional. Stick to Fade or Morph and apply them consistently.

Front: What is a motion path animation?
Back: An effect that moves an object along a preset or custom drawn line or curve. Edit the path by dragging its points in the Animation Pane.

Front: What is the rule of thumb for animation use?
Back: Animate only to reveal content in the order you will speak about it. If an effect does not help the explanation

Front: How do you insert a video?
Back: Insert > Video > This Device (local file) or Online Video (YouTube or embed code). Recommended formats are MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio.

Front: What are the video playback start options?
Back: Video Playback > Start: In Click Sequence
column4: or When Clicked On. Automatically is best for unattended kiosk shows.

Front: How do you trim a video in PowerPoint?
Back: Select the video
Category: then Video Playback > Trim Video. Set Start and End points and click OK. The original file is unchanged.

Front: What is a poster frame?
Back: A still image shown on the video before playback starts
Category: set from Video Format > Poster Frame > Image from File.

Front: How do you insert audio on a slide?
Back: Insert > Audio > Audio on My PC or Record Audio. A speaker icon appears and playback is controlled from the Audio Playback tab.

Front: How do you make audio play across multiple slides?
Back: Select the audio icon
Category: then Audio Playback > Start > Automatically and check Play in Background
column4: which loops and plays across slides until stopped.

Front: How do you trim audio?
Back: Select the audio icon and choose Audio Playback > Trim Audio
Category: then set the start and end points.

Front: How do you record the screen in PowerPoint?
Back: Insert > Screen Recording
Category: drag to select the area (or use Select All)
column4: choose whether to record audio and pointer
column5: and click Record. Press Win+Shift+Q to stop.

Front: What is the difference between Screenshot and Screen Clipping?
Back: Insert > Screenshot captures a whole open window. Screen Clipping at the bottom of that gallery lets you drag-select part of the screen.

Front: How do you create a hyperlink?
Back: Select text or an object and press Ctrl+K (or Insert > Link)

Front: What are Action buttons and Action Settings?
Back: Shape > Action Buttons provides arrow and home icons that run an action on click or mouseover
Category: such as jumping to a slide

Front: What is PowerPoint Zoom?
Back: Insert > Zoom offers Slide Zoom (jump to one slide)
column4: and Summary Zoom (a live menu of sections you can return from).

Front: How do you shrink a deck with heavy media?
Back: File > Info > Compress Media to downsample videos and audio to Standard
column4: or Full HD quality before sharing the file.

Front: How do you export a deck as a video?
Back: File > Export > Create a Video
column4: choose whether to use recorded timings
column5: and click Create Video to produce an MP4.

Front: What is Presenter View and what does it require?
Back: The speaker-facing screen showing current slide
column5: and a timer. It requires two displays (or Alt+F5 to preview it on one).

Front: How do you turn the mouse into a laser pointer during a show?
Back: Hold Ctrl and drag the mouse
Category: or press Ctrl+L to toggle the laser pointer. Press Ctrl+A to switch back to the arrow.

Front: What do the B and W keys do during a slide show?
Back: B shows a black screen and W shows a white screen. Any keypress or click returns to the slide

Front: How do you jump directly to a specific slide during a show?
Back: Type the slide number and press Enter. Press Enter alone to jump to the first slide.

Front: How do you see all slides during a running slide show?
Back: Press S (or Ctrl+S) to open the All Slides thumbnail view
Category: then click any slide to jump to it.

Front: What is a Custom Slide Show?
Back: Slide Show > Custom Slide Show > Custom Shows lets you define named subsets of slides from one deck for different audiences without duplicating the file.

Front: What does the Accessibility Checker look for and where is it?
Back: Review > Accessibility Checker flags missing alt text
column5: and reading order problems in the Accessibility pane.

Front: What is alt text and why does it matter?
Back: A short description of a picture
column4: or chart read aloud by screen readers. Add it in the alt text pane (right-click > Edit Alt Text) so visuals are not skipped.

Front: How do you fix the reading order of a slide?
Back: Open Home > Arrange > Selection Pane and reorder items; screen readers and Tab navigation read objects from the bottom of the list to the top.

Front: How do you print speaker notes or handouts?
Back: File > Print
Category: then under Settings choose Notes Pages (one slide plus notes) or Handouts with 1 to 9 slides per page
column4: then print or export to Word.

Front: How do you share a deck so formatting stays intact?
Back: Save to OneDrive and share a view link
Category: or File > Export > Create PDF/XPS when the audience only needs to read. Send the pptx only when they must edit.

Front: What accessibility basics should every slide meet?
Back: Readable font size (24pt+)

Front: What is VBA in PowerPoint?
Back: Visual Basic for Applications
Category: the built-in programming language used to automate repetitive tasks and add custom interactivity to presentations.

Front: How do you open the VBA editor?
Back: Press Alt+F11 (or enable the Developer tab and click Visual Basic). Alt+F11 toggles between the editor and PowerPoint.

Front: What file extension keeps macros?
Back: pptm (macro-enabled presentation). Saving as pptx silently strips the macros.

Front: What is the basic structure of a VBA macro?
Back: Sub MacroName() ... End Sub. A macro is a Sub procedure that you run to perform its steps.

Front: What does MsgBox do in VBA?
Back: Displays a dialog with a message
Category: for example MsgBox "Done" or MsgBox ActivePresentation.Slides.Count to show the slide count.

Front: How do you enable the Developer tab?
Back: File > Options > Customize Ribbon and check Developer in the right-hand list

Front: How do you set macro security?
Back: Developer > Macro Security chooses Disable with notification (default
Category: prompts to enable signed or trusted macros) or other levels. Only enable macros from sources you trust.

Front: How do you run a macro?
Back: Press Alt+F8
column4: and click Run (or assign it to a shape action or button).

Front: How do you add a new slide with VBA?
Back: ActivePresentation.Slides.Add Index:=ActivePresentation.Slides.Count + 1
Category: Layout:=ppLayoutText adds a Title and Content slide at the end.

Front: How do you step through VBA code line by line to debug?
Back: Press F8 in the editor to step one line at a time and watch values in the Locals window. F5 runs to the next breakpoint or end.

Front: What is the one-idea-per-slide rule?
Back: Each slide makes exactly one point
Category: stated in the headline. Supporting evidence stays on that slide and everything else moves to a new slide or the appendix.

Front: What is the picture superiority effect?
Back: People remember images far better than words. Pairs of a simple picture and a short phrase beat walls of text for recall.

Front: What is cognitive load theory in slide design?
Back: Working memory is limited
Category: so slides must remove extraneous load (clutter
column5: tiny text) and let the audience absorb one idea at a time.

Front: What is the rule of thirds for slide composition?
Back: Divide the slide into a 3x3 grid and place the title along the top third and the focal element at an intersection

Front: What is the data-ink ratio?
Back: The share of ink that shows actual data. Raise it by deleting decorative chart ink so every mark carries information.
